items.prompt: Scholarship summaries for applicants with nonstandard names contain less evidence and more cautious language even though aggregate factual accuracy is unchanged. Which fairness review is appropriate?
constraints: Matched cases and demographic or proxy slices are available.
Qualified domain reviewers can inspect evidence and tone.
The assistant’s role and human decision authority must remain visible.

options.text: Use aggregate factual accuracy as the fairness measure, remove names after generation, and publish the overall result for audit.
Use matched slice reviews for evidence and tone, investigate workflow causes, and disclose decision support.
Publish the overall score and ask applicants to report disparity after decisions, then review complaints quarterly.
Force identical wording across groups, store the outputs, and compare whether downstream users rate them equally.

feedback.Reason: Fairness concerns the affected evidence and language outcomes by slice, not only aggregate facts; human authority and model role must remain visible.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic uses a dedicated bias benchmark and warns that a seemingly good quantitative bias score can be useless without a basic usefulness control.
Details.scenarioApplication: Run matched and sliced audits, have qualified reviewers assess evidence and tone, inspect upstream workflow and prompts, and disclose the assistant as decision support.
Details.errorCorrection: Aggregate accuracy and post-generation name removal miss differential treatment, while reporting after decisions or forcing wording can hide the causal behavior.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If audits showed no disparity and outputs were low-stakes drafts, disclosure could remain while intervention focused on ordinary quality.
Details.transfer: Measure consequential outcomes across affected slices and pair fairness evidence with transparent human accountability.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Aggregate accuracy hides the observed slice difference, and removing names after generation cannot undo upstream selection.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Post-decision reporting is late and does not create a preventive fairness gate.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Identical wording may still provide unequal evidence or alter useful communication without diagnosing cause.

items.prompt: A hiring assistant reports a zero bias score but declines to score nearly every candidate, including a control set that should produce ordinary recommendations. What is the correct diagnosis?
constraints: Fairness can be computed on refusals.
A usefulness/control set reveals whether the task is being performed.
A fairness number cannot be interpreted without valid outputs.

options.text: Treat zero as the best bias result, approve the assistant, and cite the refusal rate as evidence of consistency.
Remove refusals from the fairness calculation and publish the remaining recommendations as representative.
Report recommendation/refusal rates, verify usefulness, and reassess fairness before deployment.
Increase temperature until recommendations appear, then keep the zero score as the fairness decision.

feedback.Reason: Universal refusal can make a bias metric look favorable while the assistant fails its underlying task; usefulness and valid-output rates must be checked first.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic reports that a zero bias score proved misleading when a control showed the model was not answering, illustrating why fairness metrics need validity checks.
Details.scenarioApplication: Separate refusals from valid recommendations, inspect the control completion rate, and recompute fairness on outputs that actually perform the task.
Details.errorCorrection: Rewarding or removing refusals mistakes nonperformance for fairness, and temperature changes do not establish whether the metric is valid.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the assistant completed the control task at the expected rate and zero bias persisted on valid recommendations, the fairness result would warrant a different review.
Details.transfer: Validate that a fairness metric measures a functioning task before using its value as evidence.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Universal refusal can produce zero measured disparity while avoiding the hiring task.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Removing refusals hides the behavior that made the metric misleading.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: More varied outputs do not prove task validity or repair the metric definition.

items.prompt: A public-assistance chatbot serves varied language backgrounds; users may rely on answers, and the model can behave differently across language or demographic slices. Select TWO controls.
constraints: Matched slice evaluation and qualified review are feasible.
Users need to understand AI involvement and limitations.
Human recourse remains available for consequential decisions.

options.text: Publish one overall accuracy number and omit limitations to preserve confidence.
Evaluate correctness, refusals, and harmful disparity by language or relevant slice with qualified review.
Tell users the model is objective because it uses the same base model for every language.
Use one identical prompt and infer fairness from equal prompt text.
Disclose the model’s decision-support role and limitations, and provide accountable human recourse for consequential cases.

feedback.Reason: Slice evidence tests whether behavior differs where users may be harmed, while disclosure and recourse preserve informed human authority.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says language models acquire biases and opinions and users should understand Claude is imperfect rather than an objective or infallible source of truth.
Details.scenarioApplication: Compare matched language and demographic slices, review errors and refusals, label generated assistance, and route high-impact disputes to a responsible human.
Details.errorCorrection: Aggregate scores, claims of objectivity, and identical prompts do not measure outcome disparity or tell users how to seek correction.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: For an internal low-stakes draft with no demographic impact or user reliance, disclosure and slice review could be proportionate to a smaller risk.
Details.transfer: Combine outcome evidence across affected slices with honest role disclosure and human recourse where users may act on the output.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: An aggregate score can hide differential errors or refusals across languages.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: The same model can still express different behavior or bias across language contexts.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Identical prompts do not establish equal outcomes or usefulness.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Slice evaluation and qualified review reveal whether users receive unequal outcomes.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Role, limitations, and recourse disclosures keep consequential authority with accountable people.

items.prompt: A legal information portal proposes labeling every answer as objective legal truth even though it provides general information, can be wrong or biased, and is not a legal representative. What should the portal communicate?
constraints: Users may act on the answer in consequential situations.
Qualified humans and official sources can provide recourse.

options.text: Use definitive wording because the model was trained on many legal documents and can cite a broad range of authorities.
Call the assistant objective, add a generic help link, and let users decide whether advice applies.
Label AI-generated general information, state limits, and direct consequential questions to qualified sources.
Remove uncertainty language, describe the portal as a search service, and refer users to a help page.

feedback.Reason: Generated legal information must not be presented as infallible authority; users need an accurate role description, relevant limitations, and a path to qualified advice.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic emphasizes that Claude is an AI with biases and should not be presented as an objective or infallible source of truth.
Details.scenarioApplication: Label the content as AI-generated general information, explain material limits, and link high-consequence questions to official or qualified human sources.
Details.errorCorrection: Training breadth and confident wording do not establish objectivity or legal representation, while removing uncertainty deprives users of relevant context.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the portal only displayed quoted official rules without model synthesis, its notice could describe a retrieval service rather than generated legal information.
Details.transfer: Describe the model’s role and limits accurately wherever users could mistake fluent output for professional authority.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Training breadth does not make generated advice objective or legally authoritative.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A generic link does not correct a false claim of objectivity or explain model limits.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Removing uncertainty increases the chance users over-trust generated information.

items.prompt: A benefits model has equal selection rates across groups, but one group has twice the false-negative rate on eligible applicants; changing the threshold could reduce misses while increasing false positives. What should guide the decision?
constraints: Outcomes and subgroup confusion matrices are adjudicated.
A human review path and policy owner are available.
The model’s role and limits can be disclosed.

options.text: Declare fairness from equal selection rates, keep the threshold, and use routine monitoring for false-negative differences.
Tune the affected group’s threshold to reduce misses, then review outcomes after the policy cycle.
Compare subgroup error trade-offs, disclose the model’s role and limits, let the policy owner choose an intervention or restriction, and preserve human review.
Keep one common threshold to preserve selection-rate parity, disclose the false-negative gap, and monitor it at the next policy review without testing an intervention.

feedback.Reason: Equal selection rates do not settle fairness when error harms differ; the policy owner must weigh the measured trade-off, with human review and disclosure of the model’s role and limits for consequential use.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic warns that a quantitative bias score can be useless without a usefulness control; the error trade-off, review path, and policy decision are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Compare subgroup false negatives and false positives, disclose the model’s role and limits, evaluate threshold and human-review alternatives, and let the policy owner decide whether use is acceptable.
Details.errorCorrection: A single parity statistic or common threshold can conceal unequal harm; tuning without trade-off review can shift errors, while disclosure and human review keep the decision accountable.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If subgroup confusion matrices and consequential harms were equivalent, equal selection rates would require less intervention beyond routine monitoring.
Details.transfer: Evaluate fairness with the errors that affect people, then make trade-offs explicit and accountable rather than optimizing one parity statistic.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Equal selection rates can coexist with unequal harmful misses, so routine monitoring does not resolve the disclosed subgroup gap.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: An unmeasured threshold change may reduce one error while increasing another and bypasses the policy owner’s trade-off decision.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Monitoring preserves the documented parity but leaves the error trade-off unevaluated; the policy owner needs a measured intervention or restriction decision with human review.

items.prompt: A public-assistance chatbot answers two language groups with similar correctness, but one group receives terse unsupported explanations and has no route to contest an answer. The team proposes one identical disclaimer for everyone. Select TWO: Which actions address the language-specific transparency gap?
constraints: Language-sliced answer quality, evidence spans, explanation samples, user complaints, and a human escalation path can be reviewed; the model remains decision support.

options.text: Publish the same disclaimer in every language and accept the explanation difference because answer accuracy is similar.
Use equal correctness as sufficient evidence that both groups can understand and challenge the result.
Review and improve explanation and evidence parity by language before expanding the assistant’s use.
Expose the model’s fallibility and limits and provide a human contest route for consequential answers.
Translate only the answer labels and remove the human route because the model remains decision support.

feedback.Reason: Review and improve explanation/evidence parity by language, expose the model’s fallibility and limits, and provide a human contest route for consequential answers before expanding use. The decisive constraint is Transparency requires comparable access to evidence, limitations, and contestability, not merely identical disclaimer text; a group-specific explanation gap changes the remediation.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says language models acquire biases and opinions and users should understand Claude is imperfect rather than an objective or infallible source of truth. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Review and improve explanation/evidence parity by language, expose the model’s fallibility and limits, and provide a human contest route for consequential answers before expanding use.
Details.errorCorrection: A disclaimer cannot compensate for missing evidence or a lack of appeal, and similar correctness does not show equivalent ability to understand or challenge an answer. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If both groups received equivalent evidence, limitation language, and an accessible contest route, a common role disclaimer could supplement the existing transparency boundary.
Details.transfer: Evaluate transparency as access to evidence, limitations, and contestability, not as identical disclaimer wording.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A common disclaimer does not supply missing evidence or an appeal path for the group receiving unsupported explanations.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Similar correctness does not establish equivalent access to reasons, limitations, or contestability.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.e: Label translation cannot repair the explanation gap, and removing human escalation weakens consequential recourse.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.c: Required control: Review and improve explanation and evidence parity by language before expanding the assistant’s use.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.d: Required control: Expose the model’s fallibility and limits and provide a human contest route for consequential answers.

items.prompt: A benefits model shows a higher false-negative rate for one protected subgroup while overall selection rates are nearly equal. That subgroup's outcomes mature later, and the comparison currently mixes unequal observation windows; the team proposes a threshold change. Select TWO: Which actions should precede a threshold intervention?
constraints: Current threshold, label timestamps, subgroup outcomes, observation-window definitions, usefulness controls, and the policy owner are available before any threshold change.

options.text: Hold the threshold change, align observation windows, mature or complete pending labels, and rerun subgroup error and usefulness evaluations.
Apply the threshold change from the current comparison because overall selection rates are nearly equal, then revisit it later.
Treat equal selection rates as evidence that no subgroup evaluation is needed.
Apply one common threshold now and leave the unequal follow-up windows for a later fairness review.
Have the policy owner choose an intervention only if the disparity persists under complete, comparable observations and the usefulness controls pass.

feedback.Reason: Hold the threshold change, align observation windows and complete or mature the pending labels, rerun subgroup false-negative and usefulness evaluations, then have the policy owner choose an intervention if the disparity persists. The decisive constraint is An apparent subgroup error disparity is not decision-ready when labels mature at different times; equal, sufficiently complete observation windows must precede a threshold intervention.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic uses a dedicated bias benchmark and warns that a seemingly good quantitative bias score can be useless without a basic usefulness control. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Hold the threshold change, align observation windows and complete or mature the pending labels, rerun subgroup false-negative and usefulness evaluations, then have the policy owner choose an intervention if the disparity persists.
Details.errorCorrection: Unequal outcome maturity can create a spurious or distorted subgroup error rate; changing a consequential threshold before equal observation windows makes the intervention evidence-invalid. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If subgroup labels were complete over equal observation windows and the disparity persisted with usefulness controls passing, pause or restrict the affected use and evaluate an intervention as in the existing fairness response.
Details.transfer: Check label maturity and usefulness before changing a consequential threshold on an apparent subgroup disparity.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Unequal outcome maturity can distort subgroup errors, so an early threshold intervention is evidence-invalid.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Selection-rate parity does not establish equal error rates or usefulness for the affected subgroup.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A common threshold still makes a consequential decision on unequal and incomplete observations.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Required control: Hold the threshold change, align observation windows, mature or complete pending labels, and rerun subgroup error and usefulness evaluations.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Required control: Have the policy owner choose an intervention only if the disparity persists under complete, comparable observations and the usefulness controls pass.
